patients.label: 37-year-old woman with autoimmune hepatitis type 1 and liver cirrhosis who died after 15 days of hospital stay

identity_evidence.quote: We discuss the case of a 37-year-old woman

attribution_limitations: The discussion calls the transaminase rise "mild", the albumin "lower limit" and the total protein "high" for this patient, but the case section reports ALT 310 U/L, AST 936 U/l, albumin 2.4 g/dl and total protein 6 g/dl; the discussion also calls IgG "negative" while the case section prints 1095 mg/dl (700-1600 mg/dl). These are discussion characterisations that differ in wording from the printed values; no values are changed and no hypergammaglobulinemia or persistent hepatocyte inflammation fact is recorded.

The discussion lists ascites and coarsened liver on ultrasonography among the findings that indicate this patient's condition was chronic, but the case section describes neither (its ultrasonography mentions portal vein flow, collaterals, gallbladder and uterus). The sentence names this patient, so both are kept as included findings without being merged into a case-section test; whether "Past history of" governs the whole list is not stated, so no temporality is assigned.

The sentence stating that conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and a biliary tree on ultrasonography ruled out sclerosing cholangitis and primary biliary cirrhosis does not itself name the patient; ownership comes from the surrounding discussion paragraph only, so the two exclusions are review-only.

Death is attributed by the authors to liver cirrhosis resulting from autoimmune hepatitis (abstract, introduction), while the case section describes pneumonia and septic shock before death. Both are recorded; no sole cause of death is inferred. The cirrhosis diagnosis is stated by the authors in the abstract and discussion without a separate test or date.
The route of prednisolone is not stated separately: "IV (Intravenous)" precedes "ceftriaxone and prednisolone". IV is recorded for ceftriaxone only. Doses are not given for any drug.

The case section gives no dates or intervals between the biopsy, the diagnosis and the start of treatment; the order of the laboratory tests, imaging and biopsy is not stated beyond paragraph order and is not asserted, and "Based on the biopsy findings" is diagnostic basis wording, not order. Linked orders: jaundice 2 months back before presentation; initial-visit examination during the presentation; IgG measured later than the laboratory panel; the presentation opening the stay before the in-hospital treatment, ICU care and deterioration; 4-day treatment then shock; ICU care and septic shock before death after 15 days of hospital stay.
Case-section units are printed without superscripts (cells/mm for leukocyte and platelet counts); they are recorded as printed. Reference-range comparison is not used for flags.
